    Using wayu with other shell tools

    Give each plugin and prompt one owner. Wayu can manage global entries while another tool manages project environments, themes or plugins. Keep a tool out of [tools] if its initializer already appears in your rc file.

    mise, Starship and direnv#

    Keep [prompt] enabled = false in wayu.toml when using Starship. After sourcing wayu, activate mise, initialize Starship, and install direnv's hook last:

    # ~/.zshrc, after the wayu source line
eval "$(mise activate zsh)"
eval "$(starship init zsh)"
eval "$(direnv hook zsh)"

    # ~/.bashrc, after the wayu source line
eval "$(mise activate bash)"
eval "$(starship init bash)"
eval "$(direnv hook bash)"

    # ~/.config/fish/config.fish, after the wayu source line
mise activate fish | source
starship init fish | source
direnv hook fish | source

    Use only the tools you need. On Bash login shells, source .bashrc from .bash_profile when your setup lives there. Some Fish packages already activate mise through vendor configuration; avoid a second activation. The order above makes wayu's PATH available first and places direnv after prompt-manipulating extensions, as its documentation requests.

    The pinned real-upstream suite tests these initializers together, explicit mise/direnv environment diffs when entering and leaving a fixture project, direnv authorization, and preservation of Starship's prompt definition after re-sourcing wayu. It does not certify every prompt transition, module or third-party hook. References: mise shell setup, Starship setup, direnv hooks.

    chezmoi#

    Track selected source files, not the whole generated data directory. Follow the machine-transfer guide, apply your files, then run plugin restore and rebuild runtime/scripts locally. Keep machine keys and plaintext session caches out of the source state.

    Wayu mutates entries.json and plugins.json. Capture those edits back into chezmoi before a later apply, for example with chezmoi re-add for the selected tracked files. Otherwise an apply can replace your CLI edits with an older source version. Alternatively use chezmoi's documented symlink-to-source workflow for externally modified files; wayu's atomic writer preserves such symlinks and replaces their targets. Do not sync a writer concurrently with wayu: a dotfiles manager does not participate in wayu's config lock.

    The real-upstream smoke test covers add → wayu mutation → re-add → apply. Reference: externally modified files.

    Oh My Zsh and Antidote#

    Source wayu first, then your existing manager. Keep wayu's native prompt off while retaining an external theme. Each plugin should occur in only one manager; disable wayu's built-in highlighting or suggestions when an external plugin owns that feature.

    Migrate one plugin at a time: remove it from the old manager's list, add it to wayu, and verify its completion and key bindings in a new shell before moving the next one. Keep the old configuration in version control for rollback. Neither manager's plugin-list format is a plugins.json import format.

    The pinned smoke tests load each actual manager with a local plugin and completion, then re-source wayu and verify one plugin load and retained global entries. Oh My Zsh updates are disabled in the test. This does not establish parity for every theme, plugin ordering rule or widget wrapper. References: Oh My Zsh settings, Antidote.

    Fisher#

    Let Fisher own Fisher plugins and let wayu own global entries. Keep Fisher's fish_plugins manifest alongside the selected wayu source files, and replay it with Fisher on a new machine. Do not install the same plugin twice.

    Fisher's function, completion and install-event behavior is tested with its actual pinned implementation and a local fixture plugin before sourcing wayu. Wayu's source-only Fish loader does not implement all Fisher lifecycle/theme semantics; retaining Fisher is the supported recipe for plugins that need them. Reference: Fisher.

    Sheldon#

    Keep each plugin in either Sheldon or wayu. Source wayu first, then use Sheldon's generated source or your static loader. Regenerate a static loader when changing its configuration. The pinned smoke suite checks actual source generation and loading of a local plugin alongside wayu; the benchmark records both normal and static-loader startup separately. Reference: Sheldon.

    Reproducing the evidence#

    tests/ecosystem/tools.json pins the upstream release archives by SHA-256 and source trees by full commit. To run in temporary homes:

    python3 tests/ecosystem/fetch.py /tmp/wayu-upstreams
WAYU_ECOSYSTEM_DIR=/tmp/wayu-upstreams WAYU_BIN="$PWD/bin/wayu" ruby tests/ecosystem/smoke.rb

    This network suite is separate from offline integration tests. CI runs it on macOS and Linux as a release dependency and retains the output and manifest. Missing dependencies or a failed assertion fail the job. See benchmark methodology for performance evidence and the security review brief for the separate assessment required before promoting multi-machine secrets.
